facts.statement: Walterosteus was a small arthrodire placoderm belonging to the family Selenosteidae, found in Late Devonian rocks in Germany and Morocco.
facts.quote: Walterosteus is an extinct genus of small selenosteid arthrodire placoderms known from the Upper Frasnian Kellwasserkalk facies of Late Devonian Germany and Morocco.

facts.statement: Walterosteus is classified within the family Selenosteidae and the class Placodermi.
facts.quote: Parent group: Selenosteidae Family: Selenosteidae Class: Placodermi

facts.statement: Walterosteus lived during the Frasnian stage of the Devonian period, between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 372.15 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether Walterosteus should be considered a separate genus from Enseosteus, with some researchers arguing that a specific contact between the rostral and pineal plates distinguishes it.
facts.quote: Rücklin (2011) agrees with Denison's synonymizing of Ottonosteus, but rejects Denison's synonymization of Walterosteus, claiming how Walterosteus has a contact between the rostral plate and the pineal plate, which Enseosteus does not.

rejected.statement: The genus Walterosteus was named by Erik Stensiö in 1959 to honor the German paleontologist Walter Gross.
rejected.quote: The genus was named by Erik Stensiö to commemorate the contributions done by Walter Gross, a German specialist on Paleozoic fishes, and his important contributions to the understanding of the overall anatomy of arthrodire placoderms.
